title: Tourism as a driver for jobs and growth in the Middle East and North Africa
gist: World Bank MENA Vice President Ousmane Dione argues that Middle East and North Africa tourism has proven resilient through conflict largely thanks to domestic, diaspora and regional travelers (e.g., Saudi domestic trips hit 93 million in 2025, above the Vision 2030 target), but remains below potential. He calls for treating destinations as integrated economic systems, removing regulatory and finance barriers for small firms, and using public money to mobilize private capital.

insights.claim: Tourism supports around 12 million jobs across the Middle East and North Africa, and every direct tourism job supports roughly two additional jobs in food production, transport, retail, cultural industries and other services.

insights.claim: Dione argues tourism's value lies in activity across local value chains, so destinations should be planned as economic ecosystems where infrastructure, skills, supply chains, finance, digital services and destination management work together.
